Code, Codex,"},{"id":"p3s2","text":" another DSH, a CI job, your own script — can drive it: create workspaces,
start sessions, hand the "},{"id":"p3s3","text":"DSH agent a coding task, read and write files, run commands."},{"id":"p4s1","text":"The endpoint runs *inside* the DSH host process, so a session created over MCP is a real
DSH session"},{"id":"p4s2","text":". It appears live in the DSH UI, runs inside the DSH sandbox, and is subject to
the same permission "},{"id":"p4s3","text":"policy as anything you type yourself. Nothing about the agent is
reimplemented."},{"id":"p5s1","text":"## Security"},{"id":"p6s1","text":"This endpoint is remote control of a coding agent that has shell access. Treat the token like
an SSH"},{"id":"p6s2","text":" key — and note that the plugin does too: no tool returns its value. `dsh_info` reports
where the to"},{"id":"p6s3","text":"ken comes from (a file path or the composition), never the literal, so a calling
agent's transcript "},{"id":"p6s4","text":"never accumulates the credential. A pinned token shorter than 16 characters
draws a warning at boot,"},{"id":"p6s5","text":" and a generated one is 43 characters of CSPRNG output."},{"id":"p7s1","text":"- A request that declares a body over 64 MiB is refused with `413` before the body
is read, and a ch"},{"id":"p7s2","text":"unked request — which declares no size — has its bytes counted while
streaming and is refused with t"},{"id":"p7s3","text":"he same `413` once the cap is passed (verified: 70 MB
sent chunked answered `413` in 71 ms, and a va"},{"id":"p7s4","text":"lid chunked request still works). This
is defence in depth: every tool that could carry a large payl"},{"id":"p7s5","text":"oad already has its own
cap.
- A rejected request answers `401` with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm"},{"id":"p7s6","text":"="dsh-as-mcp"`, so a standard
MCP client can tell that presenting its configured token is the fix ra"},{"id":"p7s7","text":"ther than reporting a dead
endpoint. The realm is a fixed label; the token is never echoed.
- The li"},{"id":"p7s8","text":"stener binds to `127.0.0.1` and every request is bearer-checked, including requests on
a route mount"},{"id":"p7s9","text":"ed on DSH's own web server. That check is the *only* gate there: an exact route
registered on the we"},{"id":"p7s10","text":"b server is matched **before** DSH's authorization fence — anything
unmatched is handed to that fenc"},{"id":"p7s11","text":"e as a fallback (`webserver/src/index.ts:222-227`) — so with
`http.mountOnWebServer: true` the endpo"},{"id":"p7s12","text":"int does not inherit your browser session's
protection, it enforces its own. One caveat on DSH Deskt"},{"id":"p7s13","text":"op: when ordinary browser access is
disabled there, the web server additionally refuses requests tha"},{"id":"p7s14","text":"t do not carry the renderer
header, so the mounted path is unreachable for a plain MCP client — use "},{"id":"p7s15","text":"the plugin-owned
listener. Setting `http.host: 0.0.0.0` exposes that same power to your network; the"},{"id":"p7s16","text":" plugin
warns at bind time, and you should do it only behind your own gateway.
- **The token is the "},{"id":"p7s17","text":"entire security boundary, and that boundary is your user account.** There
